sentence: This project uses mouse models to test how a neural state protein changes small cell lung cancer responses to chemotherapy and immune checkpoint blockade.
This project builds sequencing technologies to find out how extrachromosomal DNA works in cancer.
This project studies the structure of a T cell specific tyrosine kinase to learn how T cell responses are tuned by different levels of stimulation.
This project uses cell culture and mouse models to test whether DNA variants found in kidney disease patients cause disease.
This project studies how diet affects the making of indole and phenol metabolites by the gut microbiome.
This project tests whether keeping the cells that line lung blood vessels alive can reduce lung injury caused by sepsis.
This project tests a probiotic engineered to make a cytokine to see whether it protects the intestine from damage caused by ionizing radiation.
This project studies how cells from blood vessels in the brain release signals that turn astrocytes into neurons after stroke.
This project uses computational methods to map metabolic processes, especially central carbon metabolism, that guide brain development.
This project studies genetic and epigenetic reasons small tandem repeats grow longer in single brain cells in X-linked dystonia parkinsonism and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
This project builds automated tools to study how communication in genetic counseling relates to patient outcomes.
This project studies how lenalidomide, a molecular glue, works and fails in multiple myeloma, and tests a way to find other molecular glues.
This project builds a fluorescence imaging flow cytometry system that images biological samples in three dimensions at high speed.
This project studies how changes to nicotine in electronic cigarettes and oral nicotine pouches affect young people and adults.
This project studies the molecular mechanisms behind brain development, including autism, epilepsy, Rett syndrome and muscular dystrophy.
This project builds a photoacoustic computed tomography device that measures how the brain uses oxygen noninvasively.
This project builds mathematical models to predict how much drug builds up inside and outside cells, including the effect of transporters.
This project develops imaging and computational tools to measure and predict how cancers behave and respond to therapy.
This project tests whether drugs that block focal adhesion kinase, combined with other therapies, can treat melanoma that spread to the brain.
This project builds a deep learning system that pulls out and summarizes information about peripheral arterial disease from electronic health records.
